precepts.text: Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both? There is no profit in hiding the gift or the administration that God has set you in. Better is he that hideth his folly than a man that hideth his wisdom. If you know you are good at something and God has blessed you with that spirit, use it to push the truth and grow the unity God has called us to.
precepts.point: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body. A video of a church baptism in a filthy pond was shown, and the teachers had some fun with it, but this verse is not talking about getting dunked in water. Baptized means cleanse; write that down and look it up yourself. Baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water; that is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.
precepts.why:
The body has many members, and the different administrations in it are all to endeavour to keep the unity. So when we have these different administrations, we should not hide or neglect them. Sirach: “Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?”

That goes into wisdom, but also into the gift, because the wisdom God gives you comes through those gifts and through the spirit God puts on you. What profit is there in hiding wisdom or hoarding treasure? None. There is no profit in hiding the gift or the administration God has set you in and given you.

“Better is he that hideth his folly than a man that hideth his wisdom.” A man who hides his folly is better than one who hides his wisdom, who hoards up the understanding God has given him. If you know you are good at something and God has blessed you with that spirit, use it to keep pushing the truth and growing the unity God has called us to, because we are all one body and it all goes to the same Spirit.

precepts.text: There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness: the bitter bashful brother. He says yes sir to your face, and the whole time he has no intention in his heart of doing it.
precepts.point: They hold grudges, as we read in Leviticus 19; they revisit past wrongs; they lack forgiveness, as Ecclesiasticus 28 showed; and there is the quiet resentment, sitting back stewing in silence.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Another sign of bitterness is quiet resentment: they sit back and stew in silence. Sirach shows that brother: “There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness”. He is the bitter bashful brother, brother BB.

“and by accepting of persons overthroweth himself.” He'll say, man, brother, everything good. Then he is told, brother, I need you to go do this, this and this, and he says, yes sir. The whole time he is thinking, I ain't feel like doing ish for that MF. He says yes sir to your face, and he has no intention in his heart of doing it.

That is the same bitter spirit as the one that makes a man an offender for a word, only hidden. The loud one digs up evil; the bashful one smiles and resents in silence. Either way he destroys his own soul, and he overthrows himself.

precepts.text: There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness, and by accepting of persons overthroweth himself. This is for everyone who sat in that room silent; silence is agreement. Sirach 4 says do not be an underling to a foolish man. Wake up to who is leading you to destruction and separate.
precepts.point: Nobody questions these men because the souls following them are unstable and cannot go to the book and study to show themselves approved. An heart exercised with covetous practices, cursed children, which have forsaken the right way. The right way is to keep the commandments without adding an alternate reality to fit what you want.

note.label: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.why:
This one is for everybody who was in that room. Silence is agreement. If you hear that kind of talk and it doesn't compel you to say something, hey, anybody else hear that?, then everybody in that room agreed with it by sitting there and saying nothing. This scripture is for all of you who are scared to speak up.

“There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness, and by accepting of persons overthroweth himself.” That is what a lot of you are doing: too bashful to speak, accepting the person of your leader, and overthrowing yourselves. Sirach 4 says don't be an underling to a foolish man, and that is what you are doing. There is no Bible open. A man goes to jail for a lot of evil, and your leader says he is about to join him and sell his body. What is edifying about that?

Peter warned of men “beguiling unstable souls” who “have forsaken the right way”. It is time to wake up and realize who is leading you down the road of destruction, separate from them, and do the Father's will. Stop following behind brothers who want to be the new Hebrew Hammer. That is a defiled, nasty negro.

precepts.text: Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise.
precepts.point: The gifts under the tree are offerings at the heathen altar.
precepts.why:
“Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise”. Why? Because you have technology. You have Google. You can easily look this up and see it is pagan. But because we are so covetous and want that self-gratification, the gifts blind us: Thanksgiving gifts, Valentine's Day gifts, New Year's gifts, Halloween gifts, Christmas gifts, the Easter suit, your Sunday finest on Easter. Always gifts.

“And stop up his mouth that he cannot reprove.” He knows it is wrong. He knows it is evil. But he will not say anything, and he will even fight for it. Many black and brown men will battle for Christmas for hours; ask one if he is married and he says yes. So you are scared to lose a vagina. Tell your wife today, babe, Christmas is pagan, we are not celebrating it no more, and she will put a lock and key on that box, and you will never see it again. The woman has got you by the balls, gift wrapped under the tree. That is the ordinance.

So the gifts under the tree are not harmless. They are the offering at the heathen altar, and they blind the eyes of the wise and stop the mouth of the man who should reprove it.

note.label: The Religious Peer Pressure of Fred Price Jr

points: There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness, and by accepting of persons overthroweth himself. That is the perfect scripture for King Saul.

A brother broke it down: by being bashful, by not being a leader, by not obeying God's commandments, we are destroying ourselves. God is not destroying us; he gave us the plan, and we will not follow it because we are scared. Saul never believed in himself from the start. God said he was the greatest among Israel, but when he looked in the mirror he did not see the lion, he saw the kitty cat. He did not believe God. And he had help the whole time: the prophet Samuel was there to guide him, and he never listened. Had he listened to Samuel while he was there, he could have stood on his own when Samuel was gone.

Another attribute in that bashfulness is lack of counsel, because you do not want to seem stupid, uninformed, or wrong. It is one thing to make a mistake from lack of understanding; you can learn from that. It is another thing to completely forego the counsel. All Saul had to do was ask, or be patient enough to wait. That timidness causes us not to reach out or ask for help, and that compounds the bashfulness that destroys us. Why do brothers and sisters not reach out? I did not want to bother you, Cap; I know you are busy, so I just decided to do it on my own. We get that at least three times a week.

Video played on four keys to strengthening your self-esteem: one, do not speak to yourself like an enemy; your inner voice must be your refuge, never your punishment. Two, stop comparing yourself; measure only against who you were yesterday. Three, set boundaries, not because you lack love, but because you have dignity. Four, keep promises to yourself; every commitment you honor in private becomes unshakable confidence in public. When you respect yourself, the world will mirror that respect back; if you do not respect yourself, the world will pick that up and treat you as such.

Video played on shyness: everything a great communicator does is just a series of behaviors. When people say, I am shy, it is because you have been practicing the shy behaviors for 15, 20, 30 years. Confidence is another series of behaviors you can practice. It becomes part of your identity and you feel stuck, but you are not.

Video played on being uncomfortable: everything you want in life is on the other side of being uncomfortable. Break yourself of your weaknesses. It takes a man to look in the mirror and say, I have problems, and then you do not put your head down; you put your head up and start fixing them one by one. You have been comforted in your vices and your timidness for years; you have to go to war with that spirit.

A lie is a foul blot in a man, a thief is better than one accustomed to lie, and the liar's shame is ever with him. Some lie from fear, as Sarah did before the angels; others lie to deceive and destroy, and an accusation of adultery is a lie meant to kill.
Presents and gifts stop a man's mouth so he cannot reprove: that is how the church leaders are bought, with the subsidies and the grants.
Take no food from anybody at school, and especially not from your enemies. Wait until you get home.
